stem.text: Cars enter a parking garage at a rate of R(t) cars per hour, where R is a positive function and t is measured in hours. Using correct units, interpret the meaning of \( \int_{3}^{11} R(t)\,dt \) in the context of the problem.

answer_key.label: It is the total number of cars that enter the garage from \( t = 3 \) to \( t = 11 \) hours, measured in cars.

worked_solution.text: R(t) is a rate measured in cars per hour, so integrating it over time multiplies by hours and gives an amount in cars.
worked_solution.rule_named: units of a definite integral of a rate

worked_solution.text: The limits run from \( t = 3 \) to \( t = 11 \) hours, so \( \int_{3}^{11} R(t)\,dt \) is the total number of cars that enter the garage from \( t = 3 \) to \( t = 11 \) hours.
worked_solution.rule_named: integral of a rate is the accumulated change

worked_solution.text: The units are cars per hour times hours, which is cars.

options.label: It is the total number of cars that enter the garage over the whole time the model covers, measured in cars.
